newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds off highs in late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds off highs in late profit-taking.

text.p: Irish bonds lost some early gains on Friday afternoon as operators indulged in some profit-taking after a lively mornings trading, buoyed by Irish pound strength against sterling, dealers said.

"We have seen some profit-taking in the last half an hour or so. The Irish market has had a good week and we have seen a massive outperformance of Germany since yesterday and well into today," one dealer said.
"Irish pound strength against sterling has given the Irish market a boost," the dealer added.
By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 20 pence from Thursday's close at 102.00 to yield 5.96 percent having been at 102.25 an hour earlier.
The key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 50 pence from the close at 109.40 to yield 6.61 percent having touched 109.65 earlier.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 156 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and at 92 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.
The Irish pound was up to 0.9385 sterling from 0.9312 at Thursday's close.
